hook: This one is told in the second person: you are a low-clearance staffer creeping through a dark, storm-battered Site after something has gone very wrong. Expect a horror vignette first and a containment file second. Content note: the walk through the facility passes several bodies and one apparent self-inflicted death, described briefly but bluntly.
whyItMatters: SCP-3280 by S D Locke is a good example of the wiki's narrative-frame format, where the clinical report is embedded inside a piece of fiction instead of standing alone. The page sits between two neighbouring stories in a small run of linked entries, so it rewards readers who like following an author's thread. Its tags (horror, hallucination, k-class-scenario) tell you the tone it is aiming for: a monster story built around dread rather than spectacle.
thingsToNotice:
Watch how clearance levels become a plot device. The first time you open the file almost everything is blacked out, and the only way to learn more is to do something grim with a colleague's badge, so the act of reading the document is itself a choice the narrator makes under pressure.

The security-camera tour is the other piece of craft worth slowing down for: each feed is a single short tableau, and the repetition builds a picture of the whole Site without a single wide shot. Pay attention, too, to how the narration and the report gradually start to interrupt each other.
